findings.title: Nav active state incorrect on home route
findings.observation: On the home page (/), the 'Reader' nav link has data-active="true" while the 'Home' link has data-active="false". This causes the wrong nav item to appear selected.
findings.impact: Users on the hub see 'Reader' highlighted as current location, creating confusion about where they are and breaking expected active-state semantics.
findings.recommendation: Set data-active="true" on the Home link when route is exactly '/'. Ensure Reader only active on /reader and subpaths.

findings.title: No site footer present
findings.observation: The page uses min-h-screen flex-col layout on body but contains no <footer> element. Scrolling to bottom reveals no footer content, links, or legal text.
findings.impact: Missing standard site chrome: no copyright, no secondary links (privacy, about), no visual page termination. Appears incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Add a footer component with copyright, key secondary links, and consistent presence across all routes.

findings.title: Command palette (⌘K) exists but discovery relies on button hint only
findings.observation: Pressing ⌘K opens a functional command palette dialog listing routes (Home, Reader, Search, etc.). However, the only visible hint is the 'Search ⌘K' button text. No other entry point or keyboard shortcut callout is prominent on the hub surface.
findings.impact: Power users may discover ⌘K, but casual visitors have no indication of keyboard navigation or quick route access beyond the visible nav.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a subtle persistent hint (e.g., bottom-right 'Press ⌘K' toast or footer note) or ensure the command palette is mentioned in onboarding.

findings.title: Mobile nav uses 'Toggle Menu' chevron with no clear open state affordance on first tap
findings.observation: On 390px viewport, a 'Toggle Menu' button (chevron) appears in the header. Tapping it reveals additional nav items. The transition is subtle; no backdrop, label change, or expanded state indicator is immediately obvious in the captured state.
findings.impact: Mobile users may not immediately understand the expanded state or how to dismiss the menu.
findings.recommendation: Add a backdrop/overlay on menu open, change chevron to X, or add aria-expanded visual change. Consider labeled 'Menu' text at smallest widths.

findings.title: Onboarding card overlays primary CTA area on first visit
findings.observation: A 'Welcome / Start reading in three steps' card with 'Got it' and 'Dismiss onboarding' appears on the hub, partially overlaying or competing with the primary 'Open reader' and secondary CTA grid.
findings.impact: First-time visitors see competing UI; the hero value prop and CTAs are de-emphasized until they dismiss onboarding.
findings.recommendation: Consider making the onboarding less intrusive (sidebar, inline steps, or collapsible) or auto-dismiss after first interaction with primary CTA.

findings.title: Search page empty state lacks visual affordance for the search input
findings.observation: Navigating to /search shows a search input and 'Search' button, but immediately displays 'No matching articles found' with suggestions. The input is not pre-focused and no example query chips are shown inline.
findings.impact: Users land on search with no guidance on what to type and an immediate negative empty-state message.
findings.recommendation: Auto-focus the query input on load, show example chips (e.g., 'llm', 'agents'), and soften the empty message to 'Enter a query to search…' until a search is attempted.

findings.title: Hub nav includes many secondary links (Blog, Dashboard, Docs, GitHub) with no visual grouping
findings.observation: Desktop nav shows: Home, Reader, Search, For You, Sources, Topics, Blog, Dashboard, Docs, GitHub in a single inline list. No separators or grouping between core product links and secondary/docs links.
findings.impact: Visual noise; primary user actions (Reader, Search, For You) compete with secondary destinations.
findings.recommendation: Group secondary links (Blog, Docs, GitHub) to the right or in a 'More' menu. Consider moving Dashboard behind auth or to a user menu.

findings.title: Hero uses moderate scale; subhead is lengthy
findings.observation: H1 reads 'Read AI writing across the open web' at ~text-2xl sm:text-3xl. The subhead paragraph is long and may wrap heavily on constrained viewports. CTA grid below is compact.
findings.impact: Moderate visual hierarchy; could be punchier.
findings.recommendation: Consider slightly larger hero title or tighter subhead. Test with real content width to ensure no awkward wraps.

findings.title: Mobile topic pills are numerous and may require horizontal scroll or wrapping
findings.observation: On mobile, the home surface shows many topic pills (research 73, blogs 63, open-source 60, …) which wrap into multiple rows, creating a dense band before the main content.
findings.impact: Users must scroll past a wall of tags before reaching primary actions.
findings.recommendation: Collapse tags behind a 'Topics (70)' expandable, or show top N and a 'More' affordance on mobile.

passed_checks: Theme toggles (light/dark/system) are present and functional on hub chrome
Command palette (⌘K) opens and lists routes correctly
Primary CTAs (Open reader, Search, For You, Browse sources, Topics) are present and linked
Mobile 'Toggle Menu' and 'Open Search' buttons exist
Dark theme applies across viewports without obvious contrast breakage
Search page renders input controls and empty-state messaging
Viewport responsive: desktop nav hides mobile toggle; mobile shows Toggle Menu
